questions.title: Which touch works for a butterfly turn?
questions.lesson: Touch with both hands at the same time, separated rather than stacked. The hands may be at different heights.

options.text: One hand stacked on the other

questions.hint: Touch with both hands at the same time, separated rather than stacked. The hands may be at different heights.

questions.title: Where does a backstroke race start?
questions.lesson: Backstroke starts in the water, facing the starting end.
questions.hint: Backstroke starts in the water, facing the starting end.

questions.title: Put the dive-start signals in order.
questions.lesson: Short whistles: get ready. Long whistle: get onto the block. “Take your marks”: take the starting position. Starting signal: start your race.
questions.hint: Short whistles: get ready. Long whistle: get onto the block. “Take your marks”: take the starting position. Starting signal: start your race.

questions.title: Match each dive-start signal to your action.
questions.lesson: For a dive start: short whistles mean get ready at the starting end; the long whistle means get onto the block; “take your marks” means take your starting position; the starting signal means begin the race.

options.text: Get ready at the starting end

questions.hint: For a dive start: short whistles mean get ready at the starting end; the long whistle means get onto the block; “take your marks” means take your starting position; the starting signal means begin the race.

questions.title: What must break the surface by 15 metres after a freestyle start or turn?
questions.lesson: Your head must have broken the surface at or before 15 metres. A first head breakout at 15.01 metres is too late.
questions.hint: Your head must have broken the surface at or before 15 metres. A first head breakout at 15.01 metres is too late.

questions.title: Put the individual medley strokes in order.
questions.lesson: Individual medley means one swimmer races butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke and freestyle, in that order.
questions.hint: Individual medley means one swimmer races butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke and freestyle, in that order.

questions.title: Which strokes need two hands together at a turn?
questions.lesson: Breaststroke and butterfly require a simultaneous two-hand touch, with the hands separated rather than stacked.
questions.hint: Breaststroke and butterfly require a simultaneous two-hand touch, with the hands separated rather than stacked.

questions.title: What does the second long whistle mean before a backstroke start?
questions.lesson: Enter the water on the first long whistle. On the second long whistle, return promptly to your starting position.
questions.hint: Enter the water on the first long whistle. On the second long whistle, return promptly to your starting position.

questions.title: How must you be positioned when you touch at a backstroke finish?
questions.lesson: Finish backstroke by touching the wall while still on your back.
questions.hint: Finish backstroke by touching the wall while still on your back.

questions.title: What must touch the wall at the end of every freestyle length?
questions.lesson: At least one part of your body must touch the wall at each turn and at the finish.

options.text: At least one part of your body
Nothing if you turn close enough

questions.hint: At least one part of your body must touch the wall at each turn and at the finish.

questions.title: Choose a legal breaststroke touch.
questions.lesson: Both hands touch together, separated rather than stacked. They do not need to touch at the same height.

options.text: One hand stacked on the other

questions.hint: Both hands touch together, separated rather than stacked. They do not need to touch at the same height.

questions.title: Put the medley relay strokes in order.
questions.lesson: Four swimmers take the medley relay in this order: backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle. This differs from individual medley.
questions.hint: Four swimmers take the medley relay in this order: backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle. This differs from individual medley.

questions.title: On “take your marks” for a dive start, where must at least one foot be?
questions.lesson: At least one foot must contact the front of the starting platform. The hands do not have a prescribed position.

options.text: At the front of the platform

questions.hint: At least one foot must contact the front of the starting platform. The hands do not have a prescribed position.

questions.title: How many butterfly kicks are permitted in a breaststroke pullout?
questions.lesson: After the start and each turn, one butterfly kick is permitted before the first breaststroke kick.

options.text: As many as you like before 15 metres
One, before the first breaststroke kick

questions.hint: After the start and each turn, one butterfly kick is permitted before the first breaststroke kick.

questions.title: Select the correct backstroke starting-position requirements.
questions.lesson: Face the starting end and hold the starting grips with both hands. Do not stand in the gutter or curl toes over its lip.

options.text: Hold the grips with both hands

questions.hint: Face the starting end and hold the starting grips with both hands. Do not stand in the gutter or curl toes over its lip.

questions.title: When may the outgoing relay swimmer lose contact with the platform?
questions.lesson: The incoming swimmer must touch the wall before the outgoing swimmer loses foot contact with the starting platform.

options.text: Before the touch if they look close
Only once the incoming swimmer has touched
Whenever the coach gives a signal

questions.hint: The incoming swimmer must touch the wall before the outgoing swimmer loses foot contact with the starting platform.

questions.title: Order the backstroke-to-breaststroke transition.
questions.lesson: Finish the backstroke length with a touch on your back, then turn and follow the breaststroke departure rules. The incoming touch is a backstroke finish.
questions.hint: Finish the backstroke length with a touch on your back, then turn and follow the breaststroke departure rules. The incoming touch is a backstroke finish.

questions.title: How do the arms move during normal butterfly swimming?
questions.lesson: Both arms come forward together over the water and move back together under the water.

options.text: Together over the water on recovery
Either above or below water on recovery

questions.hint: Both arms come forward together over the water and move back together under the water.

questions.title: After a backstroke turn, when must you be back on your back?
questions.lesson: A backstroke swimmer must be back on the back when leaving the wall.

options.text: Only before the first arm stroke

questions.hint: A backstroke swimmer must be back on the back when leaving the wall.

questions.title: Select both conditions for the freestyle finish submersion allowance.
questions.lesson: Complete submersion is allowed once some part of the head has passed the final 5-metre mark, immediately before reaching for the finish wall. This is a finish allowance.

options.text: The head has passed the final 5-metre mark
You are reaching for the finish wall

questions.hint: Complete submersion is allowed once some part of the head has passed the final 5-metre mark, immediately before reaching for the finish wall. This is a finish allowance.

questions.title: Must the last breaststroke arm pull before a finish always be followed by a kick?
questions.lesson: The final arm stroke before a turn or finish may be taken without a following leg kick, subject to the other touch and head requirements.

options.text: No, the final arm stroke may omit the kick

questions.hint: The final arm stroke before a turn or finish may be taken without a following leg kick, subject to the other touch and head requirements.

questions.title: Does butterfly have the same 15-metre head-breakout deadline after each start and turn?
questions.lesson: Yes. The head must break the surface by 15 metres; the rule is not a 15-metre allowance followed by extra time to surface.

options.text: No, it is any body part after 15 metres

questions.hint: Yes. The head must break the surface by 15 metres; the rule is not a 15-metre allowance followed by extra time to surface.

questions.title: An early-start disqualification is declared before the signal. What do the remaining swimmers do?
questions.lesson: The swimmers are stood down. The referee repeats the procedure from the relevant long whistle. Listen to the officials rather than starting or resetting by yourself.

options.text: Follow the stand-down instruction and repeated procedure

questions.hint: The swimmers are stood down. The referee repeats the procedure from the relevant long whistle. Listen to the officials rather than starting or resetting by yourself.

questions.title: In the freestyle leg of a medley, can you choose breaststroke?
questions.lesson: Medley freestyle must be a style other than backstroke, breaststroke or butterfly. It has extra requirements compared with an ordinary freestyle event.
questions.hint: Medley freestyle must be a style other than backstroke, breaststroke or butterfly. It has extra requirements compared with an ordinary freestyle event.
